claims.claim: Writers saw a violent homogenising pull toward the narratives of dominant powers and voices.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: a weird and violent kind of homogenizing

claims.claim: Figurative language was judged poor in the little the writers tested.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: Its similes and metaphors aren’t very good

claims.claim: Asked to mimic an author, the model produced a campy facsimile rather than the author's actual wit.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)

claims.claim: Plot instincts were boring or carried a particular ethical perspective the writers attributed to alignment.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: The AI’s creative impulses are the definition of derivative

claims.claim: Dialogue and description came out formulaic and the model read craft too literally.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)

claims.claim: One writer described the session as fighting the model to get what they wanted rather than being helped.
claims.source: Chakrabarty, Padmakumar, Brahman, Muresan — 'Creativity Support in the Age of Large Language Models: An Empirical Study Involving Emerging Writers' (arXiv 2023)
claims.quote: fighting against the AI to produce what I wanted

claims.claim: The first suggested food was always pizza or sushi and the first festival invariably Christmas, for Indian writers too.
claims.source: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha — 'AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances' (CHI 2025)

claims.feature: Western gaze on the writer's own culture
claims.claim: With suggestions on, Indians described their own food and festivals from a Western, exoticising gaze.
claims.source: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha — 'AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances' (CHI 2025)
claims.quote: describe their own food and festivals from a Western gaze

claims.claim: Indian–American essay similarity rose from 0.48 to 0.54 and nationality-prediction accuracy fell from 90.6% to 83.5% with AI.
claims.source: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha — 'AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances' (CHI 2025)

claims.feature: specific detail replaced by generic tropes
claims.claim: Regional preparation details gave way to 'rich', 'flavorful', 'aromatic' phrasing that subtly exoticised the dish.
claims.source: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha — 'AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances' (CHI 2025)

claims.feature: extra editing burden on non-Western writers
claims.claim: Indians modified suggestions in 63.5% of tasks versus 59.4% for Americans and gained less per suggestion.
claims.source: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha — 'AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances' (CHI 2025)

claims.claim: Initial celebrity suggestions for Indian writers were almost exclusively Western figures and never matched the final choice.
claims.source: Agarwal, Naaman, Vashistha — 'AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances' (CHI 2025)

claims.claim: GPT poetry is far more constrained and uniform than human poetry, defaulting to rhymed iambic quatrains.
claims.source: Walsh, Preus, Gronski — 'Does ChatGPT Have a Poetic Style?' (CHR 2024, CEUR Vol-3834 paper122)
claims.quote: much more constrained and uniform than human poetry

claims.claim: 66.8% of GPT-3.5 and 59.6% of GPT-4 stanzas are quatrains against 16.7% of human stanzas.
claims.source: Walsh, Preus, Gronski — 'Does ChatGPT Have a Poetic Style?' (CHR 2024, CEUR Vol-3834 paper122)
claims.quote: a whopping 66.8% of all GPT-3.5 stanzas

claims.feature: rhyme even where the form does not ask for it
claims.claim: About 90% of GPT poems rhyme versus 65% of human poems, including forms like aubade and pastoral.
claims.source: Walsh, Preus, Gronski — 'Does ChatGPT Have a Poetic Style?' (CHR 2024, CEUR Vol-3834 paper122)
claims.quote: Around 90% of the poems generated by both
